title: Design 3D-printable parts by describing them
summary: A developer built SOMA, an app where coding agents like Claude Code design 3D-printable parts as code; he reports very good results in this early prototype.
agent_role: The agent writes and edits the Python model code and runs build, analyze and render commands. It also produces drawings and animations. The human describes the part, inspects it, measures it and marks fixes.
outcome: The author reports mostly testing with Claude Code and Claude Opus 5.5, with very good results. It is an early 0.8.0 prototype.
what_they_did: A developer built a desktop app that works with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini. The agent gets a SOMA tool and a file of project rules. The user describes a part, such as a Raspberry Pi 5 case with vents in the lid, in PETG plastic. The agent writes design code that SOMA redraws after every change. The user clicks, measures or sketches on the 3D view to ask for fixes, then saves files ready to print.
how_it_went: The author says he mostly tested it with Claude Code and Opus 5.5, with very good results. It is labelled an early prototype, version 0.8.0. The app itself was largely written by coding agents.
worth_knowing: The download is over 1 GB and is not signed by a trusted publisher. It is mainly tested on Windows, and you need your own paid agent subscription.
prompt: Design a parametric 3D part in CadQuery: [describe the part, e.g. a case for a [device] with vents], to be printed in [material] on [printer]. Make key dimensions adjustable parameters. Build the model, check wall thickness and overhangs, and render a preview. Summarise the dimensions and any printability concerns. Wait for my feedback before exporting to STL.

curation.rationale: An original maker workflow: a CLI coding agent writes CadQuery models while the app builds, renders and analyses them for feedback. Code and a concrete loop are available, but there are no documented project outcomes beyond the author's 'very good results'.
